# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
THE 3 OUT OF 10, and it is two failures, not one.

FAILURE A: EVERY JUDGED ESTIMATE WAS WRONG BY 4 TO 5 TIMES, ALL FAST.

  Tag cut and pushed      forecast by 02:00   actual 00:27   ~4x
  Install rehearsed       forecast by 04:00   actual 00:45   ~5x
  Whole release path      forecast 8 hours    actual ~90 min ~5x
  Full battery            forecast 10-20 min  actual 12.5m   ACCURATE

The ONLY accurate estimate was the one measured from a previous run of the
same command. Everything judged was wrong, and wrong in one direction.

Root cause: the estimates were sized in "how long would a careful person take"
units. Wrong unit. The cost driver for an agent is WRONG TURNS, not typing,
and wrong turns are bounded by how well specified the task is, not by its
size. A well-specified task is far faster than it looks; a vague one is far
slower.

FAILURE B, THE SERIOUS ONE: THE NIGHT HAD NO DEPTH.

Thirteen tasks is a plan for the WORK, not a plan for the NIGHT. They finished
in ninety minutes and nothing was queued behind them. The founder said it
plainly: the plan would have stopped work during the night if he had gone to
bed. Roughly six of eight hours would have produced nothing.

A PLAN WHOSE COMPLETION LEAVES THE MACHINE IDLE IS NOT FINISHED BEING WRITTEN.
An overnight plan is not a list of what must happen. It is a queue deep enough
that finishing early is impossible.

FAILURE C, mine and unprompted: I front-loaded the release because it was the
legible, provable thing, and left the four items the founder actually named
(collaboration, toolkit, memory, connectors) with no design work at all. The
easy provable work crowded out the work he asked for. That ordering was never
stated as a decision, which makes it a silent skip.

OTHER MISTAKES TONIGHT, each corrected:
1. Tagged the wrong commit; the manifest was split from the version bump.
   Caught by a pinned test. Cost a soft reset of three commits.
2. First version of the fence fix converted EVERY session string, breaking
   five CLI tests that legitimately pass short labels. Narrowed to the
   canonical harness shape. No test was weakened.
3. Reported handover-ack as missing when I had run it against the wrong tool.
4. Two shell scans printed their label instead of their result, because head
   exits 0 regardless.
5. Claimed a landing while its deciding gate was still running. The stop hook
   caught it and was right.
